report:
## Verdict: REJECT (one Important finding: an unreleased changelog fragment still says verify-memory is not supported under a rule-set file)
This PR is not ready to merge yet. The code and tests meet the criteria, but `changelog.d/389.added.md` still says `sqllens verify-memory` is not supported, and criterion 19 requires that sentence to be corrected by a separate PR that merges before this one.
Rule applied: rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `changelog.d/389.added.md` line 10 still says "`sqllens verify-memory` is not supported". This PR adds `changelog.d/400.added.md`, which says verify-memory now runs under a rule-set file, so the next release notes would contradict each other. Criterion 19 requires a `codex/changelog-notes-<reason>` PR to correct that sentence and merge before this PR; neither this diff nor the head view shows that correction. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: release-note fragment read by no tool for behavior; published release notes reach readers outside the repository, so capped at Important -->

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/eval/runner.py`: `_verification_metadata` sets `loaded.catalog.confirmed = True` again, outside the state lock, after `confirm_catalog` in `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` already set it under the lock when the check passed. The line is redundant and suggests the runner owns that state. (raised by 2/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/eval/runner.py` lines 120-180: `VerificationIdentityError.kind` is a plain `str`, not a `Literal` of the five documented kinds, and `describe()` falls through to the refused/catalog message for any kind it does not recognize, so a typo or a new kind would render a message with `None` values instead of raising. (raised by 1/6 agents)
- VC-12: FAIL (suggestion) — Changelog asserts every golden case runs as a query_database request under the identity and the command stops with exit 1 naming the refusal and the values used [changelog.d/400.added.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  changelog.d/400.added.md:6-8 says the pre-case check stops with exit 1 'naming the refusal and the values it used'. In src/sqllens/eval/runner.py:151-176 describe() names values (rule set, account, user) only for kinds 'refused' and 'catalog' (lines 170-175). Kind 'no_rule_set_file' (154-158), 'missing' (159-164) and 'account_required' (165-169) print only the refusal text with no values used, e.g. passing --user without --rule-set, or omitting --user, or omitting --account with several bound accounts. cli.py:652-657 prints that describe() message with exit 1, so those refusals exit 1 without naming values. Counterexample: a missing --user prints only 'a rule-set file is configured, so --user is required'. The claim is overbroad: values are named only for selection-refused and catalog failures. Exit 1 and the refusal name hold for all kinds.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred

- VC-46: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — When this issue's PR merges, no fragment in `changelog.d/` on `main` says `sqllens verify-memory` is not supported or not available under a rule-set file. Today `changelog.d/389.added.md` says "`sqllens verify-memory` is not supported"; while that fragment is unreleased, its sentence is corrected through a `codex/changelog-notes-<reason>` PR that merges before this issue's PR. [changelog.d/389.added.md:10]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Graded with criteria.json (counts: every element is a {criterion, text} object, criterion 19 matches). The criterion is about main after the PR merges and is satisfied through a separate codex/changelog-notes-<reason> PR that merges first. In the head view, changelog.d/389.added.md:10 still says "`sqllens verify-memory` is not supported", and the diff touches only changelog.d/400.added.md, which says verify-memory now runs under a rule-set file. The head view cannot show whether the separate PR has merged, so the state of main after merge cannot be settled. Other fragments mentioning verify-memory (210.added.md, 313.fixed.md:13) do not claim it is unsupported under a rule set. Missing evidence: the merge status of the codex/changelog-notes PR and the content of 389.added.md on main at merge time.

  </details>
